question: Test whether the unweighted boundary action supplies the Whitney shear-port equalizer.

objects.definition: Square face circulation divided by squared face area
objects.units: inverse fourth power of side length before weighting
objects.basis_orientation: oriented b and coorientation to ordinary flags

sources.section_or_object_id: Whitney curl Gram and centered rotational energy

assumptions: Regular Euclidean cell, unit edge-circulation Whitney one-forms and common face averaging.
Cooriented flag identification and closed skew port from v0.10.
Coefficient-one comparison uses the declared nondimensional unit side length.

technique_plan.technique: Stokes, barycentric moments and rational Gram replay
technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: compare literal and equalizing action weights

clock_receipt.update_rule: constant skew exchange using action metric
clock_receipt.period_claim: sqrt(6/53) excludes an exact common half phase

dynamics_readout.state_space: ordinary E+T2 edge current and auxiliary flag coordinates
dynamics_readout.initial_boundary_conditions: one closed cell, no initial flag stock

fitted_parameters_or_formula_choices: literal unit weight tested, c=ell^2/48 comparison
target_exposure.search_domain_and_budget: unit, unaugmented and equalizing weights; no empirical fit

calculation_steps: Compute derivative energy by Stokes and replay wedge product
Apply the weighted flag Gram to E and T2
Compare unit-weight frequency ratio against the half-stock criterion

result.scope: The literal unit-cell curl energy supplies 16/3, 48 times the required 1/9. Squared rates are (4/3,106/9) and exact common half transfer is impossible for this port.

counterexamples_and_failures: Literal unit term overshoots the cancellation by a factor of 48
limitations: No native relative coefficient, physical length, second-stage latch or deficit allocation
next_discriminant: Test whether native transport fixes a relative length-squared weight independently of spectral equalization, or use sector-resolved latches.
